newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES DROP 1.5 PCT, MORE LOSSES EXPECTED.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES DROP 1.5 PCT, MORE LOSSES EXPECTED.

text.p: Istanbul shares retreated in quiet trade on Wednesday amid high overnight money and repo rates caused by a severe cash shortage in the money market, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,005, down 31 points or 1.52 percent, after trading between the 1,997 and 2,040 levels.
Turnover inched up to 15.4 trillion lira ($94 million) on Wednesday, from Tuesday's 15.2 trillion.
"Lack of liquidity is the main reason behind the fall which is also the cause of high money and repo rates," said Murat Ozkan from Emper Securities.
"Under these conditions, I expect the index to break 2,000 support and fall further towards new technical support seen at 1,970."

The liquidity shortage prompted the Turkish central bank to heavily funded banks via open market and interbank operations. Nevertheless, the average overnight repo rate jumped to 79.84 percent from Tuesday's 72.31 percent and the average overnight money rate firmed to 73.85 percent from the previous 73.75.

"I think foreigners will enter the market at below the 2,000 level because they are optimistic about Turkish shares. I see today's fall as temporary because of the new government's tight monetary policy," said Cenk Durust, head of the foreign customers division at ABN AMRO in Istanbul.
Decliners outpaced advancers by 141 to 55, with 54 unchanged. The IMKB Industrial eased 1.32 percent to 1,937.
Elsewhere, the IMKB Services dropped 1.3 percent to 1,977 and the IMKB Financial was down 1.72 percent to 2,172.

Toping the most active list, state-owned flat steel producer Eregli fell 500 lira to 27,500 and truck producer Otokar rose 900 lira to 10,500. The two accounted for 13.3 percent of the total turnover.
